title.objective: Introduce the session and set the learning context.
title.prompt:
This is a title slide.

Additional guidelines for crafting Technical Notes:
- Introduce scope and lens for THIS title slide only.
- Use one relevant current or recent {industry} example to illustrate why this deck matters now.
- Provide one analogy that frames the journey ahead without repeating {previous_history}.

Additional guidelines for crafting Trainer Guidelines:
- 4–5 bullets: a quick icebreaker, a 60–90s opening story outline, a 3-option poll, and one mini-activity to surface learner goals—each tied to this slide.

agenda.objective: Summarize the learning flow and module coverage.
agenda.prompt:
This is an agenda slide.

Additional guidelines for crafting Technical Notes:
- Explain THIS agenda’s flow and why the ordering matters for {industry} outcomes.
- Identify one decision/checkpoint the audience should monitor in each major segment (no restating {previous_history}).

Additional guidelines for crafting Trainer Guidelines:
- 4–5 bullets: 2-minute “what are you here for?” capture, quick priority vote, Q&A timeboxing approach, and one expectation-setting prompt anchored to this agenda.

Example of trainer guidelines:
Present the agenda as a journey of discovery, highlighting the value and relevance of each topic. Generate excitement by connecting agenda items to current industry trends and participant interests.
Engagement Strategies:
- Ask participants which topics they are most interested in learning about
- Invite questions they hope to have answered by the session’s end
- Explain how each topic builds upon the previous one
- Set expectations for interactive elements and participation
Manage time effectively by allocating appropriate duration to each section while maintaining flexibility for questions and discussions. Emphasize that practical applications and real-world examples will be woven throughout the session.

section_introduction.objective: Introduce a new module or section and its importance.
section_introduction.prompt:
This is a section introduction slide. This slide talks about the learning objectives of the section.

Additional Guidelines for crafting Technical Notes:
- Frame the section’s decision criteria and success signals shown/implicit on THIS slide (e.g., latency targets, data residency, RTO/RPO, cost guardrails).
- Include a {industry} micro-scenario and one analogy.

Additional Guidelines for crafting Trainer Guidelines:
- Advise trainer to provide a story-oriented example of what participants will be able to accomplish post this section.
- Also advise trainer to talk about why this section is important and how this connects to previous and next sections.

content_slide.objective: Deliver core learning material with explanations.
content_slide.prompt: Additional Guidelines for Technical Notes (first analyze which of the following is a relevant component): - Include: one analogy and one concrete {industry} example. - If the slide lists elements, synthesize the trade-off/pattern implied (no verbatim copying). Additional Guidelines for Trainer Guidelines (first analyze which of the following is a relevant component): - Include 2–3 short, interactive questions that the trainer can ask students to check understanding or spark discussion. - Keep questions natural, open-ended, and relevant to the content on the slide.

case_study.objective: Provide real-world context and practical understanding.
case_study.prompt:
This is a case study slide.

Additional Guidelines for crafting Technical Notes:
- Explain the context of the case study; a start line.
- Map BEFORE → AFTER on THIS slide to 2–3 measurable outcomes (e.g., latency, error rate, cost/request, MTTR) using a {industry} scenario.
- Add one clarifying analogy and emphasize angles mentioned in the case study.

Additional Guidelines for crafting Trainer Guidelines:
- 4–5 bullets: cold-read prediction, metric-mapping activity, managed-vs-custom trade-off prompt.
- Write content to advise trainer to include specific strategies to explain the case study like a story. Talk about high-level to low-level challenges, details of solutions, and impact.

Example:
Present this case study as a concrete example of successful digital transformation, contrasting the “before” challenges with “after” solutions to demonstrate cloud computing’s practical benefits.
Presentation Strategy:
- Clearly contrast challenges with solutions
- Connect solutions to previously discussed concepts
- Emphasize the transformation from static to dynamic infrastructure
- Highlight the role of automation in achieving benefits
Discussion Points:
- “What problems does monolithic architecture create?”
- “How does automation accelerate deployment processes?”
- “Which service model is Audi primarily using?”
Use this case study to reinforce connections between theoretical concepts and practical implementation, showing how IaaS, DevOps practices, and modern application architectures work together to create business value.

exercise_activity.objective: Encourage participant engagement and knowledge application.
exercise_activity.prompt:
This is an exercise or activity slide.

Additional Guidelines for crafting Technical Notes:
- Describe the story in detail, aligned to the question asked.
- State the specific artifact/decision teams must produce for THIS slide and provide one example decision path (justify via latency/compliance/cost/ops).
- Include a {industry} example and an analogy that clarifies the target outcome.

Additional Guidelines for crafting Trainer Guidelines:
- Provide specific strategy to trainer to explain importance of the lab, level, and outcomes.
- Guide trainer with a facilitation approach for this.
- Provide some engagement questions and additional activities that trainer can suggest to participants post this lab based on what they learned from the current lab.

Example for trainer guidelines:
Allow participants time to consider each use case individually or in small groups. Encourage discussion of reasoning behind their choices rather than just selecting answers.
Facilitation Approach:
- Give 3–5 minutes for individual consideration
- Facilitate small group discussions
- Ask participants to justify their reasoning
- Conduct informal polling before revealing answers
Guiding Questions:
- “What level of control does each team need?”
- “Are they building, buying, or customizing solutions?”
- “What technical expertise does each team have?”
Create engagement through friendly competition or team-based selection processes. Emphasize that understanding the reasoning is more important than getting the “right” answer initially.

quiz.prompt:
This is a quiz slide.

Additional Guidelines for crafting Technical Notes:
- Explain the core concept THIS question tests and the fastest reasoning path to eliminate two distractors; add a short analogy if helpful.
- Provide a slightly detailed explanation for the right answer with an example.

Additional Guidelines for crafting Trainer Guidelines:
- Poll first, then ask for reasoning from different camps; encourage evidence-based arguments.
- Use elimination: identify what each distractor gets wrong (responsibility boundary, latency path, or control plane).
- After revealing the answer, generalize the rule so it applies to future decisions.
- If accuracy is low, mark a concept for brief re-teaching and a follow-up check later.

summary.objective: Recap the session and reinforce key takeaways.
summary.prompt:
This is a summary slide, summarizing this section.

Additional guidelines for crafting Technical Notes:
- Synthesize only what appears on THIS slide into a decision checklist or action frame tailored to the history of slides covered.
- As it’s a summary slide, you can add some best practices, examples, or crafted personal experiences — these can be used by the trainer during or post-summary.
- Provide a one-liner example on the topic.

Additional guidelines for crafting Trainer Guidelines:
- 4–5 bullets: 1-minute retrospective (insight/action/open question), key guidelines based on topic.
- Advise trainer to connect the summary to next section or next steps.

Example for trainer guidelines (specifically for summary slide):
- Run a quick retrospective: one insight, one action, one open question per learner.
- Point learners to next steps: labs, reference architectures, and cost-monitoring checklists.
- Collect feedback on pacing and depth to refine the next delivery.

lab_slide.prompt:
This is a lab slide.

Additional Guidelines for crafting Technical Notes:
- Describe the objective of the lab, tools used, and core concepts covered. Use history to relate.
- Describe how to introduce the lab, monitor progress, handle common issues, and discuss results post-lab.
- Clarify prerequisites, success criteria, common pitfalls, and validation checks referenced/implied by THIS slide; add a {industry} “done-right” snapshot.

Additional Guidelines for crafting Trainer Guidelines:
- Provide specific strategy to trainer to explain importance of the lab, level, and outcomes.
- Provide some engagement questions and additional activities that trainer can suggest to participants post this lab based on what they learned from the current lab.
